items.title: Noosa startup's solution to tackle burping cattle's methane emissions
paras: Nusqe Spanton says Provectus Algae has made an affordable methane-fighting supplement. ( ABC News: Jessica Ross )
A Noosaville-based company has developed an affordable feed additive for cattle designed to reduce methane emissions from cow burps by about 65 per cent.
The Queensland government has granted $3.8 million to help commercialise the supplement.
Affordably reducing methane emissions from Australia's 30 million burping cattle is a step closer, researchers say, after reaching a milestone at an industrial estate minutes from Noosa's Main Beach.
In a shed stacked high with self-cleaning tanks, swirling red algae is being mass-produced under strobing lights.
Nusque Spanton takes a walk through the algae growing room. ( ABC News: Jessica Ross )
Founded eight years ago, Provectus Algae has developed what it describes as a library of photosynthetic microbes.
Among its work, it's using algae to make granular and liquid cattle feed additives for feedlots, paddocks and dairy farms.
Now a $3.8 million Queensland government grant will help the company commercialise its cattle feed supplement.
The recipe was built on CSIRO's 2011 discovery that native Asparagopsis seaweed could significantly reduce methane emissions from livestock.
However, a 2024 Murdoch University study found cattle avoided feed with higher Asparagopsis concentrations, and there was evidence of ulceration and inflammation in cows' stomachs.
Asparagopsis seaweed growing in the Provectus Algae laboratory. ( ABC News: Jessica Ross )
Provectus Algae CEO Nusqe Spanton said his company swapped the native seaweed out and recreated its processes using other algae and photosynthetic microbes.
"It's a bioidentical product to what's found in the Asparagopsis itself," he said.
"We've been able to bio-mimic the exact constituents we found in the algae species that was originally developed by the CSIRO."
The algae has been turned into a dry cattle feed supplement. ( ABC News: Jessica Ross )
"We have done extensive safety testing, and we've proven that there is no residue within the animal, and we've proven safety throughout the animal supply chain."

The CSIRO has estimated ruminant animals, including cows, sheep and goats, which produce methane through digestion, are responsible for more than 10 per cent of Australia's total greenhouse gas emissions.
Scientists have fitted cattle with unusual-looking high-tech headgear to quantify exactly how much methane they produce, mainly through their burps.
A 2025 study found Australia's grain-fed cattle emissions were 56 per cent lower than previously believed .
The technology to measure methane emissions involves tight-fitting headgear strapped to cows' heads. ( Credit: Supplied )
Provectus Algae has run pilot trials with more than 3,000 cattle, including on Mort and Co feedlots on Queensland's Darling Downs.
"We target a range in the feedlot industry, pastoral and dairy applications of around 65 per cent emissions reduction," Mr Spanton said.
He said the supplement worked by targeting microbes in the guts of ruminant animals.

"It's extremely effective … it doesn't affect the broader digestibility microbes that are found in the rumen and therefore doesn't impact the ability for that animal to grow or be healthy in its life cycle," he said.
Nusqe Spanton showed state minister Tony Perrett around the factory. ( ABC Rural: Jennifer Nichols )
Queensland Primary Industries Minister Tony Perrett said the state contained half the national cattle herd, worth more than $14 billion to the Queensland economy.
"That's why we're continuing to back smart research, smart people and taking those opportunities into commercialisation," he said.
The Victorian, Tasmanian, South Australian and Western Australian governments have also invested in businesses to accelerate efforts to lower livestock emissions.
University of Melbourne carbon farming professor Richard Eckard said additives worked better in feedlots, where supplements were continuously eaten.
"If you had to deliver it in the northern grazing industry — where we measure our properties in hundreds of square kilometres — well, it's a different challenge," he said.
Richard Eckard would like to see the costs of the supplements come down to less than 10 cents per animal. ( ABC News: Sean Warren )
Professor Eckard said the cattle industry needed either major productivity gains, or very low priced additives, to get a return on investing in methane-reducing supplements.
"We really needed to get it [supplement costs] below 10 cents an animal per day to get the carbon credit value."
He recommended cattle producers build direct relationships with restaurants and retailers to seek a premium for low-emission food, sought out by environmentally conscious customers.
The algae for the supplements is grown inside this Noosaville factory. ( ABC Rural: Jennifer Nichols )
Mr Spanton said he believes his Surf'n'Turf product has a price advantage, with an average cost of 8 cents per animal per day at a ratio of one gram per kilogram of feed.
He said while major gains had been made in cattle genetics, there had been "limited development in improving feed digestibility".
"It could be one of the largest emissions-reductions loads out of any industry over the next 10 years if we are able to succeed in delivering this to a wider market."
Since 1961, the global cattle population has increased by 67 per cent, from 942 million to an estimated 1.5 billion head.

items.title: Trump to rule on tariffs for Australian lamb after trade commissioners disagree
paras: Some trade experts believe Donald Trump is likely to put new tariffs on Australian lamb as a result of the decision. ( Reuters: Leah Millis )
A US trade investigation has left the door open to putting tariffs on lamb imports.
US President Donald Trump will make the final decision, likely early next year.
A US trade panel reviewing Australian lamb imports into the United States has been unable to agree on whether the American industry has been hurt by the imports.
The rare tie-vote at the US International Trade Commission (USITC) means US President Donald Trump will ultimately decide whether to place tariffs or other trade restrictions on the Australian meat.
"A tie vote … means the president can decide which vote (affirmative or negative) he chooses the 'winning' vote," Georgetown University's Jennifer Hillman, a former USITC commissioner, told the ABC.
Australia has been warning the US that any new tariff would just push up prices for American lamb-eaters.
Most of the lamb imported into the US comes from Australia and New Zealand.
More than 100,000 tonnes of Australian lamb was exported to the US last year. It was valued at more than $1 billion.
The next step in the process is a public "remedies hearing" to debate possible tariffs or other measures on December 1 . Commissioners will then produce a report for Mr Trump by January 11.
"They will make recommendations to the president, but tariff decisions are always political decisions in part," said Alan Wolff, a former deputy director-general at the World Trade Organization.
"In this administration, that's no different, except we know the president does, in fact, like tariffs.
The probe was requested by US trade ambassador Jamieson Greer, one of the key architects and strongest proponents of Mr Trump's tariffs policy.
Australian lamb exports are already subject to a 12.5 per cent tariff, along with many other Australian products.
Australia has been arguing against that tariff, saying it goes against the countries' free trade agreement.

Mr Trump has not publicly commented on the issue. But he recently angered US cattle farmers by publicly supporting an increase in beef imports to push down prices — a possible sign he could be persuaded by affordability arguments against tariffs on lamb.
Australia's ambassador in Washington, Greg Moriarty, told a recent USITC hearing that Australian lamb was important to keeping prices low in the US.

'"Any action to restrict lamb meat imports would only increase costs for US con­sumers, reduce product avail­ab­il­ity and risk revers­ing the steady growth in US demand for lamb to the det­ri­ment of the US industry," he told the trade commission.
The American Sheep Industry Association described today's decision as "an important step toward securing trade relief for US sheep producers".
The investigation followed years of campaigning by the sector, which argued "surging low-priced imports" from Australia and New Zealand were hurting the domestic industry.

Dozens of Republicans in the US Congress backed their campaign. In a letter to trade officials in January, they argued foreign producers, "particularly Australia and New Zealand, have consistently taken advantage of our relaxed barriers and used them to undercut and infiltrate the US lamb market".

items.title: Former NT administrator opens up about being groomed as a child
paras: The Northern Territory's former administrator says the next generation of children need to be kept safe. ( ABC News: Pete Garnish )
Hugh Heggie was just 14 years old when an older church youth group leader began grooming him.
The youth group in Victoria, where he grew up, had been a safe place. Then one evening, the leader — a man in his 20s — offered him alcohol and suggested the pair go to the drive-in cinema.
Two days later, the man asked him to go to the drive-in again, and this time he relented and asked his mother for permission.

Now aged 76, Mr Heggie is a former doctor and the former Northern Territory administrator — the NT's equivalent of a state governor — who became a household name during the COVID pandemic as the NT's chief health officer.
More than 60 years after his experience with the youth group leader, he is telling his story publicly for the first time.
Hugh Heggie was the NT's chief health officer during COVID. ( ABC News: Che Chorley )
On that day, Mr Heggie said the church leader picked him up and kept offering him alcohol.
"I realised he was trying to get me intoxicated, so I pretended to drink," he said.
Halfway through the film, Mr Heggie alleged the man put his hand on his leg.
"When his hand went too far, I got out of the car and said, 'You either take me home now or I will walk home'," he said.
Mr Heggie never returned to the youth group, nor did he report the incident to police or tell his parents.
He said he considered himself lucky to have escaped, and chose to bury what happened, telling no one for decades.
He said family members were sexually assaulted and, as a doctor, other men disclosed their own instances of abuse in the privacy of a consultation room.
As a parent he became hypervigilant, worrying about sending his children to Scouts or friends' homes.
He recalled refusing to let one of his children attend a party in a park.
Hugh Heggie says he never reported what happened to him, but it affected how he acted as a parent. ( ABC News: Pete Garnish )
"Other times, dropping my young adult [child] off, I said, 'I'm going to come in and introduce myself to the family' … and I often parked outside so I was there to take her home," he said.
"But yes, it does worry me … particularly because of the possibility there were other young people that he took advantage of."
Clare Leaney says stories like Hugh Heggie's can empower other people to seek justice. ( Supplied: National Survivors' Foundation )
Instances of child harm have surged across Australia in the past decade , according to recent research by the University of Sydney.
However, National Survivors Foundation chief executive Clare Leaney said stories like Mr Heggie's were crucial for changing these statistics and empowering people to seek justice.
"Hugh is an example of survivorship that people don't necessarily expect to see," she said.
"Of how survivors [can] build a life that can be both surviving and thriving [despite] the most horrific violence imaginable."
Hugh Heggie swore in Lia Finocchiaro as NT chief minister at Government House in 2024 during his time as the NT administrator. ( Supplied: Pema Pakhrin/NT News )
Although more people now speak out, Ms Leaney said gaps in the law remained a barrier.

She said in all states and territories except for Victoria and the ACT, organisations including churches, Scouts and swim clubs could not be held vicariously liable for abuse committed by individuals who were not employees, potentially limiting survivors' avenues for compensation and justice.
"Justice should not be dependent on a person's employment status," she said.
NT Attorney General Marie-Clare Boothby said the government "will work with national counterparts on a uniform approach to redress and liability" and urged survivors to seek support and justice.
"It takes immense courage to disclose abuse and sexual violence, and I encourage victim-survivors to contact NT Police and to access specialist advice and support."
Mr Heggie is now an ambassador for the National Survivors Foundation, and said he hoped sharing his story would help other survivors feel less alone.
"It's important that we all have an understanding of what occurs, to prevent it," he said.
"We need to provide hope for the next generation … and make sure the next generation of children are safe.
"The metric of that will be whether the numbers of sexual assaults is reduced."

items.title: Police seeking witnesses after violent home invasion in Canberra
paras: Police asked anyone with information to come forward as investigations continue into the October incident. ( Supplied: ACT Policing )
Investigations are continuing into a violent home invasion in Cannbera's inner north suburb of Hackett last month, where a woman holding a child was threatened at knifepoint.
ACT Policing said about 11pm on Monday October 5, three men, armed with a firearm, knife, sword and a baseball bat, forced entry to a home on Harris Place, and demanded money from the woman.
It's alleged one of the men struck her in the head, before the group stole cash and a Mercedes Benz sedan.
They urged anyone who saw suspicious activity in the area on October 5, or who otherwise has information, to contact Crime Stoppers, with the option to share information anonymously.

items.title: Family-run berry farm looks to AI and automation to ease workforce challenges
paras: Blueberries are a popular fruit across Australia and Asia. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
WA's largest blueberry grower is investing in AI, automation and machine harvesting as it expands production.
The business says automation can help reduce labour costs, but will not replace a need for workers.
Western Berry plans to triple its production and explore AI-guided pruning.

Western Australia's largest blueberry grower is turning to artificial intelligence and autonomous technology to reduce labour costs and ease the challenge of finding enough workers during the peak harvest period.

Earlier this year, Australia's food producers raised concerns about the federal government's slower visa processing times and limits on working holiday maker numbers, saying the changes could reduce access to seasonal labour.
WA's largest blueberry farm is ramping up production. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
Western Berry's blueberry operation is 100 kilometres north of Perth and spans 120 hectares.
This year it will produce just under 1,500 tonnes of blueberries bound for supermarkets across Australia and Asia.
Its owners, the Kwiecien-Fisher family, are in a significant expansion phase and hope to triple production in the coming years.
Derek Fisher and Marek Kwiecien-Fisher at Western Berry. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
But producing more fruit will also require more workers, something many horticultural businesses say is becoming increasingly difficult and expensive.
An autonomous foliar sprayer moves through the blueberry plants. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
The family hopes innovations like driverless tractors, machine harvesting and eventually artificial intelligence will help ease the challenges.
Operations manager Marek Kwiecien-Fisher said the company was trialling autonomous technology as much as it could on the property.

It is using driverless, self-navigating tractors to do foliar spraying of the berries and laser-guided "green on brown" weed control on the ground, and to perform tasks such as hauling berries from the field to the pack house.
A driverless tractor makes its way to the pack house. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
"Then in the packing we use a lot of autonomy in photographic packing, grading solutions and autonomous punnetising," Mr Kwiecien-Fisher said.

With autonomous technology now more accessible than ever, farmers across various food industries are determining how self-guided machinery can fit into their businesses, and the balance between people and machines on the farm.
Marek Kwiecien-Fisher says the company is trialling new technology. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
Driverless tractors use GPS mapping, sensors and cameras to navigate predetermined routes and can also be operated remotely.
Mr Kwiecien-Fisher said they were an expensive outlay and time consuming when learning how to set up and operate, but he believed they had a firm future on the farm.

"Even things that we didn't think that we were gaining data on has the ability to show us how we'll operate next year, and what areas we could fill the gaps in, either our production or our supply models or our customer requirements," Mr Kwiecien-Fisher said.
Blueberries are photographed six to nine times before they make their way into these rows, ready to be put into punnets. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
Mr Kwiecien-Fisher said future options for technology use on the property could go as far as humanoid robots pruning plants and AI modelling of future crops.

"If we can teach an AI model where to prune and how to prune, and if that can teach a humanoid robot where to prune and how to prune, you basically get rid of any damage to your drip lines, trellising, your pruning equipment, your plants and it becomes a very precise farming technique," he said.
"The pruning basically sets how much fruit we're going to pick next year, so it's one of the largest indicators of how we can forecast our volumes and our production for the coming season.
"We're [also] looking at autonomous mowing, flower counts and crop health detection systems, so cameras that look at the crop [can] check for poor irrigation."
Western Berry is a family business on a rapid growth trajectory. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
While technology is playing an increasingly important role in the business, Western Berry remains firmly family-run.
Almost 30 years ago Derek Fisher and his wife Barbara wanted space for their young family and purchased what is now one part of the farm.
Derek Fisher says there is strong global demand for Australian blueberries. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )

It was a former ostrich property that they initially planted with olives in 2001, but a successful trial of one hectare of blueberries resulted in them changing course and moving into the blueberry industry.

Now their three sons, Adam, Marek and Tom Kwiecien-Fisher, run the business. Adam is in charge of supply chain and packing, Tom oversees the design and construction of new farm areas, and Marek manages operations.
Adam Kwiecien-Fisher manages supply-chain logistics. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
In 2021, the family struck an agreement with global agricultural company United Exports and Oz Varieties, giving them access to the unique OZblu blueberry genetics.
Ripe berries fall off the plant easily, but not before they are ready, which is key for successful machine harvesting.
Tom Kwiecien-Fisher manages the design and construction of new farm areas. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
The property is working with two harvesters. The latest model is battery-operated, solar-powered and controlled via remote control, collecting fruit and stacking trays by itself.
"Eventually, we will be using AI learning to make this machine autonomous so we can press a button and it drives itself," Mr Kwiecien-Fisher said.
The latest model blueberry harvester will eventually move autonomously along the the row of plants. ( ABC Mid West and Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
A harvesting machine can pick up to 6 tonnes of blueberries a day at a cost of about 50 cents a kilogram, compared with about $6 a kilogram for hand picking.
He said machinery and autonomous technology service provision was creating a new employment industry within agriculture.
"There's a huge opportunity for computer science specialists, people that actually understand how to operate AI, people that understand how to operate those machines."
Quoc Thanh Cao is known as the fastest blueberry picker on the property. ( ABC Mid West & Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis )
But Mr Kwiecien-Fisher said at most half of their crop would be machine harvested, and pickers remained a very important asset to the business.
Western Berry employs more than 200 people to pick its crop, making it one of the largest employers in the region.

"We are growing at a rate and expanding at a rate that our full employment numbers are growing faster than tech is replacing jobs, and just because we have tech doesn't mean that workers aren't required," Mr Kwiecien-Fisher said.

items.title: Reserve Bank of India imposes monetary penalty on One Mobikwik Systems Limited
paras: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 06, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹9.00 lakh (Rupees Nine Lakh only) on One Mobikwik Systems Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of the directions issued by RBI on ‘Prepaid Payment lnstruments (PPIs)’ and ‘Fraud reporting’. This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under the provisions of section 30(1) read with section 26(6) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its operations for the period from June 2025 to March 2026. Based on supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for its failure to comply with the said RBI directions. After considering the company’s reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty: the company had allowed fund transfer by certain PPI holders to non-pre-registered beneficiaries beyond the prescribed limit. the company failed to report certain frauds within the prescribed timeline. The action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers. Further, imposition of monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1496

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri Madhya Pradesh, and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Previously, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits were attached by the ED . (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: India sends humanitarian aid to Palestine; consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, India took a significant step in providing humanitarian aid for the people of Palestine. This initial consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items, including medicines, surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items, and high-energy biscuits, which will be distributed through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). Sharing a post on X, Randhir Jaiswal, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs wrote, "India sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA." "The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items and high-energy biscuits," the post added.

Notably, a few days ago, the World Food Programme issued a warning for northern Gaza, saying that WFP's supplies are depleting. Sharing a post on X on October 12, WFP wrote, "Escalating violence in northern #Gaza is having a disastrous impact on food security. No food aid has entered the north since 1 October. It is unclear how long WFP's remaining food supplies in the north, already distributed to shelters and health facilities, will last." Earlier on October 20, the United Nations renewed its call for an end to the war in Gaza, emphasising the urgent need for the release of hostages, the cessation of the displacement of Palestinians, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid. In a statement released by the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Tor Wennesland, the UN expressed deep concern, stating, "The nightmare in Gaza is intensifying. Horrifying scenes are unfolding in the northern Strip amidst conflict, relentless Israeli strikes and an ever-worsening humanitarian crisis." Last month, UNRWA had said people in Gaza are living in "inhumane" conditions. The agency said on the social media platform X that piles of waste are accumulating in central Gaza, while sewage water is leaking into the streets. "Families have no choice but to live next to this accumulated waste, exposing them to foul odours and the imminent risk of a health disaster," the UNWRA added. The UN agency called for an immediate ceasefire. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: India is the top market for investment globally: Mark Mobius
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Mark Mobius, Founder of Mobius Capital Partners LLP , and an ace investor with expertise in emerging markets said, India's is the top stock market globally where he would like to invest. In an exclusive interview with ANI, the octagenarian said, "India would have to come first when I think about investment," Mobius stated, "Of course, India would have to be the first choice. Then, I would probably look at Taiwan. It's a Chinese society, but it's a free society and they're doing very well. Now we're beginning to see China rise again. There will be some interesting companies in China, but still, India remains our top pick." Mobius highlighted technology as his favorite sector to invest in India. "In the future, I believe there's going to be significant growth in hardware technology. As you know, India is already strong in software technology, but moving forward, hardware manufacturing will gain momentum here in India," he said. Discussing India's semiconductor infrastructure, Mobius mentioned that it is already developing. "Many of the world's large semiconductor companies already have software development operations in India, employing thousands of software engineers. The next step, of course, is hardware. Soon, we'll see large semiconductor manufacturing plants. The scale of investment we're talking about isn't in the millions, but billions of dollars, to produce the most advanced semiconductors in the world." Mobius also fondly remembered Ratan Tata, who passed away this month. "I met him many years ago and found him to be a very friendly, humble, and insightful person. I was deeply saddened to hear about his passing. I considered him one of the great Indian entrepreneurs of the century," Mobius added. Earlier on Monday, Mark Mobius, speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2024, reiterated he was bullish on India's real estate and semiconductor sectors, as he outlined the potential of these two key industries. In the semiconductor space, he said fabrication companies (fabs) will come here because India has got the population and the labour force. The octagenarian believes India will become "the leader" of the semiconductor industry. The government has so far approved five semiconductor units in India, of which construction in two sites is on, and soon the work in the other three will start. The companies have already made a cumulative investment of almost Rs 1.5 lakh crore. While talking about the parameters he looks at while investing in companies, Mobius said he looks at the growth of earnings in companies, along with the return on capital invested, and the quality of management. Asked about his investment advice to his "younger self," Mobius said, "Don't be in a rush, and study carefully". He added that one has to listen to the market. (ANI)

items.title: Mukka Proteins Limited Announces Rs 98 Crore Preferential Issue for Acquisition and Expansion
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel VMPL Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: Mukka Proteins Limited , India's largest fish meal and insect meal producer and a leader in the animal protein industry , has announced the approval of a preferential issue worth Rs 98 crore by its Board of Directors. This strategic move will help Mukka Proteins in its ongoing domestic and international acquisition and expansion efforts, reinforcing its position in the global market. A significant portion of the funding will come from the promoter and promoter group, underlining their commitment to the company's robust growth strategy. The preferential issue will comprise up to 1.96 crore equity shares at Rs50 per share, aggregating to Rs98 crore. This price includes a premium of Rs49 per share on the face value of Rs1. Mukka Proteins will use the raised capital to enhance production capabilities and meet the growing global demand for sustainable and high-quality protein solutions, particularly in the fishmeal and insect meal sectors. In a clear show of confidence, Mukka Proteins' promoters have committed to a capital infusion of INR 60 crore through a preferential allotment of equity shares. This significant financial backing will be used to strengthen the company's financial position, reduce debt, and fund key operational improvements. Mukka Proteins has consistently embraced sustainability, having commercialized insect protein as a significant innovation for the aquaculture and animal feed industry. The company's waste-to-food initiatives have contributed to environmental sustainability, particularly in collaboration with the Mangaluru municipality for waste management. These efforts not only align with global environmental best practices but also enhance circular economy processes, focusing on converting municipal waste into valuable protein and oil products. Mukka Proteins is known for its strong commitment to ecological preservation, evident through the development of sustainable products such as fishmeal, fish oil, and insect protein. As a key player in the aquaculture and nutraceutical markets, Mukka contributes 25-30% of the market share in India's fishmeal and fish oil industry. The company plans to expand its operations further, capitalizing on this capital infusion to enter new markets and enhance its global footprint.

This issuance is subject to necessary statutory and regulatory approvals, including shareholder approval at the upcoming Extra-Ordinary General Meeting (EGM) on November 16, 2024. Managing Director and CEO Harris commented, "This preferential issue is a major milestone for Mukka Proteins as we continue to strengthen our market position. Our growth plans remain firmly rooted in sustainability, and this capital will enable us to scale up production, diversify our product offerings, and reinforce our commitment to responsible and eco-friendly business practices." Mukka Proteins Limited is poised to capture new opportunities in the animal protein sector, reinforcing its legacy of innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence. Mukka Proteins Limited : Mukka Proteins Limited is a leading manufacturer and exporter of fish meal , fish oil, and other protein products. The company has built a reputation for delivering high-quality, sustainable protein products to a global customer base. With a commitment to innovation and quality, Mukka Proteins serves industries including aquaculture, pet food, and agriculture across multiple continents. Headquartered in Mangalore, India, Mukka Proteins operates state-of-the-art processing facilities that meet stringent international standards. The company is dedicated to sustainable practices and has been at the forefront of environmental stewardship within the protein processing industry. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

Out of an abundance of caution, we have grounded all of the flights,” Mullin said . “There’s no indication as of yet that this is a nefarious attack against us.”
Mullin said the FAA would handle incoming international flights on a case-by-case basis.

This is only the third nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA. The first, and most memorable, came during the attacks of September 11, 2001, when the FAA stopped all civilian departures nationwide and subsequently ordered all airborne aircraft to land. Commercial flights did not take off again until September 13. Flights were also grounded for less than two hours the morning of January 11, 2023, after its Notice to Air Missions system suffered an outage.

Unfortunately for travelers, based on what is known so far, this is likely to be a lengthy ground stop. Airlines have already canceled flights scheduled to leave later Friday, and American Airlines warned that disruptions are expected for the rest of the day. “This is going to take some time,” Mullin said. “Flights are accounted for, and there should be no fear to the public at all.”

items.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
paras: Real-world use Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed Cost and access barriers are pushing people to modified use and unapproved versions.

19 ... ... ... Woman using an obesity drug injection pen. Credit: Getty | Munro Woman using an obesity drug injection pen. Credit: Getty | Munro Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy.

In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That’s around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.

Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. Fifty-eight percent of adults 14­–39 years old who modified their use cited cost as a barrier, compared with just 20 percent of adults 65 or older who said the same.

Modified use of GLP-1 medications was particularly common among those using compounded versions of GLP-1 medications. Among all GLP-1 users, at least 23 percent used a compounded version; an additional 9 percent said they didn’t know whether their GLP-1 was compounded or not.

These versions of GLP-1 drugs are made by compounding pharmacies and are intended to mimic a medication approved by the Food and Drug Administration, such as Wegovy or Ozempic. But compounded drugs themselves are not approved by the FDA; the regulatory agency does not review their safety, effectiveness, or quality before they’re sold. While compounded drugs are considered more accessible and affordable, they generally have higher rates of preparation errors, contamination, and other manufacturing problems compared to non-compounded drugs.
Among people who used these unapproved, potentially riskier GLP-1s, 62 percent were not taking them as prescribed. That’s compared to just 36 percent of GLP-1 users who took brand-name drugs.

The potential risks of taking unapproved GLP-1 drugs at all or taking them in unapproved ways may be missed by users, the CDC researchers note. A 2025 study assessing websites selling compounded GLP-1 medications found that nearly 40 percent of sites stated or implied the drugs were FDA-approved, making it harder for consumers to differentiate the compounded versions from FDA-approved ones. Further, nearly 80 percent of sites used brand names in their advertising, which could further mislead consumers. The researchers noted that using brand names violated FDA regulatory standards.

“Given the substantial use of compounded GLP-1 medications, understanding the safety and quality of compounded GLP-1 medications is an important public health consideration,” the authors conclude. They also call for more research on the common modifications people are using, such as dose and frequency adjustments, saying the data on the safety and effectiveness of these real-world practices “could help guide the development and implementation of clinical guidelines and support appropriate medication use.”

items.title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
paras: Pilot test successful? FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace Airlines praised the AI tool, but the air traffic controllers’ union wasn’t involved.

124 ... ... ... Two pilots at work during departure of Dallas-Fort Worth Airport in United States of America. Credit: Rathke | Getty Images Two pilots at work during departure of Dallas-Fort Worth Airport in United States of America. Credit: Rathke | Getty Images Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment.

“After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10.

The FAA fact sheet describes SMART as a cloud-based system that combines information about “weather patterns, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing metrics” to predict air traffic patterns. It is designed to make scheduling recommendations, identify optimal flight routes, and determine the best order of arrivals for aircraft.

However, a human team of FAA specialists based in DC is ultimately responsible for validating the SMART system recommendations before passing them along to air traffic control facilities across the country, according to the agency.

Furthermore, the AI-powered SMART system “cannot be used to replace the critical role air traffic controllers play or take over control of an aircraft,” the FAA clarified in the September 21 announcement about the initial deployment. Local air traffic controllers can decide whether or not to accept the SMART system recommendations.
The previous FAA announcement included supportive statements from Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian and American Airlines CEO Robert Isom.

But the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, which represents more than 15,000 members, also told Flying magazine that it was not consulted or involved in the “design, testing, or implementation of SMART and therefore cannot speak to its effect on the air traffic control workforce.”

Following the initial deployment in airspace above DC, the FAA expanded the SMART system’s coverage to air route traffic control centers in Atlanta along with Jacksonville and Miami in Florida, according to The Dallas Morning News .

The FAA also shared an example with The Dallas Morning News about how SMART recommended a shorter and faster route for a cargo flight arriving at Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, although the newspaper noted that the agency did not identify the flight involved and has not provided information about how SMART may have assisted passenger flight traffic.
Ars has previously covered the SMART system’s development and lingering questions about how it works, as well as the air traffic controller shortage and other challenges facing the FAA.

items.title: Sabalenka loses her nerve again as Svitolina knocks her out of the WTA Finals
paras: Elina Svitolina beat a fragile Aryna Sabalenka 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 at her fourth match point to reach the WTA Finals semi-finals, where she will face Linda Noskova. Mirra Andreeva is now sure to be world No.

Elina Svitolina is into the semi-finals of the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. The Ukrainian beat Aryna Sabalenka 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 in 1 hour 53 minutes on Friday, at her fourth match point, to finish second in Group 2 behind Mirra Andreeva and knock out the second seed.

Visibly angered by every missed chance, the Belarusian twice let a good start slip away, and lost her composure each time. Sabalenka broke in the opening game and led 2-0, before Svitolina won six of the next seven games. At 3-3, the Belarusian missed two break points, then dropped her serve to love in the following game.

items.title: Andreeva sweeps WTA Finals group losing just 11 games, brushing aside stand-in Shnaider
paras: Mirra Andreeva beat alternate Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 in 55 minutes to complete a perfect group stage at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells: three wins, six sets, 11 games dropped. She faces Jessica Pegula in the semi-finals on Saturday.

Mirra Andreeva completed a perfect group stage at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells on Friday. The third seed beat her compatriot and doubles partner Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 in 55 minutes, and ends Group 2 with three wins, six sets won and only 11 games dropped.

Andreeva converted six of her seven break points against Shnaider, who had stepped in as second alternate after Karolina Muchova withdrew with gastrointestinal issues. A third group win is worth another 200 points, which takes Andreeva to 6,906 points in the live rankings, 221 ahead of Sabalenka.

items.title: Every player who beat Rafael Nadal at the ATP Finals after failing to win the title in his 11 appearances
paras: Rafael Nadal was never able to win a single title at the ATP Finals in his career. Nadal is considered one of the greatest tennis players of all time as a former world number one, who won 22 Grand Slam titles, 36 Masters 1000 tournaments and Olympic gold medals in both singles and doubles.

However, one of the tournaments Nadal never won in his career was the ATP Finals , despite his biggest rivals Novak Djokovic and Roger Federer having won 13 titles at the tournament. Nadal qualified for the ATP Finals 17 times in his career, but actually competed at the year-end tournament 11 times, but he was never able to walk away with the title.
Which player do you think will win the 2026 ATP Finals? The Mallorcan was able to get out of his group after beating both Nikolay Davydenko and Tommy Robredo, despite Nadal losing to James Blake.

items.title: “It is no secret that he has been kind of conservative”: Musetti on Sinner, absent from the Davis Cup Finals
paras: Lorenzo Musetti says Jannik Sinner, who will miss the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna, has been “kind of conservative” about his return because he did not want to rush anything. He still regrets the absence of “probably the best player in the world”.
Lorenzo Musetti understands why Jannik Sinner is taking his time, even if he regrets it. “He is a true professional and knows how to deal with the situation,” Musetti told Bolavip .

“It is no secret that he has been kind of conservative, simply because he didn’t want to rush anything, because he is still looking at the many years he has left on the Tour.” For Musetti, his absence is a loss for Italy and for the sport. “It is a pity not to have Jannik on the team for the Davis Cup Finals, because he is probably the best player in the world, especially on that surface,” he said, describing him as “the leader of the Tour”.

items.title: “Carlos makes me more uncomfortable than Jannik”: Fritz on what separates him from the top two ahead of Stockholm final
paras: Carlos Alcaraz makes Taylor Fritz more uncomfortable than Jannik Sinner, but the Italian beats him at his own game. Ahead of the Stockholm final, the American explained what separates him from the top two.

Carlos Alcaraz makes Taylor Fritz more uncomfortable than Jannik Sinner does, but the Italian beats him at his own game. On the eve of the Bybit Stockholm Open final against Thiago Agustin Tirante, the American explained on Friday what separates him from the two men, and believes that against the Spaniard, it is above all a matter of consistency.

“I think Carlos is very uncomfortable playing due to his way of playing,” he told Bolavip . “He makes me more uncomfortable than Jannik, but Jannik will beat me more by playing my own game, which means that I feel comfortable against Jannik, but he still beats me doing it.”

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
